scheme_name: Distribution of Seeds of more productions varieties/ Hybrids varieties Seeds and fertilizer at subsidies etc. to Adivasi farmers in Tribal Area: Castor cake/Neem cake/ Liquid Fermented Organic Manure / Green manure seed (For mix in the soil) Gujarat
description:
The Distribution of Seeds of More Production Varieties and Hybrid Varieties Seeds and Fertilizer at Subsidies to Adivasi Farmers in Tribal Areas is a significant welfare scheme initiated by the Government of Gujarat.

This scheme was launched in the year 2019 as part of the broader initiative to enhance agricultural productivity among tribal communities.

The primary objective of this scheme is to improve the agricultural yield of Adivasi farmers by providing them access to high-quality seeds and fertilizers.

The scheme specifically aims to increase the production of various crops through the distribution of hybrid seeds and organic fertilizers.

The target is to cover approximately 50,000 Adivasi farmers across the tribal areas of Gujarat.

The scheme focuses on crops such as castor, which is a significant cash crop in the region.

Farmers are provided with hybrid seeds that are known to yield higher production compared to traditional varieties.

The government provides a subsidy of up to 50% on the cost of these hybrid seeds.

For instance, if the market price of hybrid castor seeds is INR 3,000 per kilogram, the farmer would only pay INR 1,500 due to the subsidy.

Additionally, the scheme includes the distribution of neem cake and castor cake, which are organic fertilizers that enhance soil fertility.

Farmers receive these organic fertilizers at a subsidized rate of 30% off the market price.

The market price for neem cake is typically around INR 1,200 per quintal.

Thus, with the subsidy, farmers can purchase neem cake for approximately INR 840 per quintal.

The scheme also promotes the use of liquid fermented organic manure, which is essential for sustainable farming practices.

Farmers are encouraged to use green manure seeds that can be mixed into the soil to improve its quality.

The green manure seeds are provided to farmers free of cost under this scheme.

Eligibility for this scheme is specifically targeted at Adivasi farmers residing in designated tribal areas of Gujarat.

Farmers must possess a valid landholding certificate to qualify for the benefits of this scheme.

The age limit for eligibility is set at a minimum of 18 years.

There is no upper age limit specified for participation in the scheme.

Additionally, farmers must be registered under the local agricultural cooperative societies to avail of the benefits.

The application process for this scheme involves several steps.

Farmers must first approach their local agricultural extension officer to express their interest in the scheme.

They are required to fill out an application form that includes personal details and landholding information.

The necessary documents include a copy of the landholding certificate and an identity proof such as an Aadhar card.

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the agricultural extension officer.

Upon approval, farmers receive a notification regarding the allocation of seeds and fertilizers.

The distribution of seeds and fertilizers typically occurs during the pre-monsoon period to align with the planting season.

The timeline for the distribution is usually set between April and June each year.

Farmers are encouraged to utilize the seeds and fertilizers promptly to maximize agricultural output.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Agriculture, Government of Gujarat.

Farmers can contact the local office of the Department of Agriculture for queries and assistance.

The contact details for the Department of Agriculture can be found on the official Gujarat government website.

This scheme is part of a larger effort by the Government of Gujarat to promote sustainable agriculture and improve the livelihoods of tribal communities.

The government has allocated a budget of approximately INR 50 crores for the implementation of this scheme over the next five years.

Statistical data indicates that the average yield of castor in Gujarat is around 1,200 kg per hectare.

With the introduction of hybrid seeds, the expected yield can increase to approximately 1,800 kg per hectare.

This increase in yield is projected to significantly enhance the income of Adivasi farmers.

The scheme also aims to educate farmers about sustainable agricultural practices.

Workshops and training sessions are organized to teach farmers about the benefits of organic farming.

The use of organic fertilizers is expected to reduce dependency on chemical fertilizers.

This aligns with the government’s vision of promoting environmentally friendly farming practices.

The scheme has received positive feedback from farmers who have reported increased productivity.

Farmers have noted improvements in soil health and crop resilience due to the use of organic fertilizers.

The government monitors the progress of the scheme through regular assessments and feedback from beneficiaries.

The success of the scheme is evaluated based on the increase in crop yields and farmer satisfaction.

In conclusion, the Distribution of Seeds of More Production Varieties and Hybrid Varieties Seeds and Fertilizer at Subsidies to Adivasi Farmers in Tribal Areas is a crucial initiative aimed at empowering tribal farmers in Gujarat.

By providing access to high-quality seeds and organic fertilizers, the scheme seeks to improve agricultural productivity and enhance the livelihoods of Adivasi communities.

The comprehensive support structure in place ensures that farmers receive the necessary resources and education to succeed in their agricultural endeavors.
